card.title: Same Memory, Different Meaning
card.instruction: Return to one shared memory as comfort, then evidence, then accusation, changing its meaning without abandoning the facts.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You kept my first terrible painting. That used to feel wonderfully loyal.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I still have it in the hall.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you believed in me before anyone else.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It makes visitors appreciate your later work.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Ah. My earliest humiliation has become your introduction to the house.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before my exhibition, I keep thinking how you hung my first painting. It makes me feel safe here.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Still in the hall. I point it out to everyone.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: So that's proof you believed in me before the reviews.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I tell them even you had to start somewhere.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You hung it to reassure everyone else they couldn't possibly do worse.

mechanism: A treats a preserved first painting as comfort, then proof of belief, then evidence of humiliating comparison.
confusable: Unlike a generic grievance, the same hanging and display must retain its facts while its meaning changes.
comparison: S223-b reinterprets an early painting before an exhibition; S223-a reinterprets a saved seat.

bindingFindings.assessment: Not safely rebindable unchanged. The retained a seed and corrected b seed preserve the shared seat and first-painting material, but b's supplied binding hash identifies its original rather than this revision. The photograph action, changed-smile opening, retelling response, unchanged-photograph challenge and second-meaning closing preserve fixed facts without establishing the full comfort–evidence–accusation progression. All four supporting seeds, their distinct sourceHash fields, card content versions and both D226 instructions and dialogues were read. D226-a supplies the overseas-job/shop choice; D226-b supplies the keep/return spare-key choice. Bespoke a's seedRefs and exact seedUse fit its seat and job/shop reinterpretation toward possible accusation. Bespoke b adapts the key binary to keeping or selling the painting, but its exact seedUse claims movement toward possible accusation while B4's exhibition-funding offer and A5's sacrifice interpretation move toward renewed support. Correcting the single does not repair that existing provenance mismatch. Both pairs' dialogue, seedRefs, seedUse, reviewedCardFingerprints, exampleVersion and editorialStatus remain unchanged. Transfer cardId, fingerprint, seed IDs, original binding hashes, substitution slots and compiled-pair-draft status are preserved. This is a binding assessment, not a new pair review; the prior incompatibility reservation remains unresolved.
